Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

Since "No Signal" plus data disabled is showing, let's work through the device settings. Please check these for me, one at a time:

**1. Airplane Mode** — Swipe down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings panel. Do you see an airplane/plane icon that's highlighted or colored in? If it is on, please tap it to turn it **off**. When Airplane Mode is on, it shuts off cellular, Wi-Fi, and data all at once — which matches exactly what you're describing.

**2. Mobile Data** — In Settings → Connections (or Network & Internet) → Mobile Networks, is the "Mobile Data" toggle switched on? You mentioned data looks disabled, so let's make sure that's turned on.

**3. Reboot** — I want to confirm this one: did the phone fully power down and restart after I restored the line, or was it more of a quick screen off/on? A full restart is needed for the phone to re-register on the network.

Can you check those three things and tell me what you find? Once I know whether Airplane Mode is on or off, I'll know which direction to go next.

turns.thought:
That's exactly the right catch — **"SIM Card Status: missing"** is almost certainly the remaining piece of this puzzle. It means the phone isn't detecting the SIM card at all, which is why you see "No Service" and why the data indicator shows as disabled even though the mobile data toggle is on. Your account and line are fine; the phone just can't read the card that identifies you on the network.

This usually happens when the SIM has shifted slightly out of its tray — it can work loose over time from normal handling.

**Here's what I'd like you to do — reseat the SIM card:**

1. **Power the phone all the way off.** Don't skip this — removing a SIM while the phone is running can cause problems.

2. **Locate the SIM tray.** On the Smartphone Pro Max it's a small pinhole tray on the edge of the phone (usually the side). You'll need a SIM eject tool — the small metal pin that came in the box — or a straightened paperclip works fine.

3. **Eject the tray.** Push the pin gently but firmly into the pinhole until the tray pops out slightly, then pull it out the rest of the way.

4. **Take the SIM card out of the tray.** Check both the gold contact surface on the SIM and the tray slot for any dust, lint, or debris. If the contacts look dirty, you can gently wipe the gold surface with a clean, dry, soft cloth. Don't use liquids.

5. **Set the SIM back into the tray** making sure it's seated flat and snug — it should sit flush and not rock or wobble. The notched corner lines up with the notch in the tray so it only fits one way.

6. **Push the tray back into the phone** until it clicks fully flush with the edge.

7. **Power the phone back on** and give it a minute or two to find the network.

Once it's back on, check whether the signal bars come back and whether the SIM status now reads as active instead of missing.

**One thing worth noting:** your device supports eSIM, and your SIM was last replaced/transferred on **2025-01-20**. If reseating doesn't restore the signal, that would point to the SIM card itself having failed rather than just being loose — in that case it would need to be replaced or moved to an eSIM profile, and I'd need to get you over to our technical support team to set that up.

Go ahead and try the reseat and let me know what the status shows afterward.

Here's a quick recap of what we did today:

- **Root cause #1 (no service):** Line 555-123-2002 was suspended due to overdue bill B1234321. That $65.00 payment is now **Paid** and the line is **Active**.
- **Root cause #2 (still no signal after activation):** The phone showed "SIM Card Status: missing" — the SIM wasn't seated properly. Reseating it restored your **excellent 5G signal** and **data**.

A couple of housekeeping notes to keep you out of trouble going forward:

- **February statement B1002 — $150.00, due 2025-02-19.** It's currently Issued, so getting that in before the 19th is exactly the right plan.
- **Data usage:** You're at 8.7 GB of your 15 GB allowance for the cycle ending 2025-02-28, so you've got room left.
- **If the SIM loosens again** — if reseating becomes a repeated fix, that's a sign the tray or card is worn and should be swapped out properly. Just reach out and we'll get it handled.
- **Line 555-123-2003 (L1003)** is still suspended whenever you want to take a look at that one.

Have a great day, and thanks for your patience working through the steps!
